~Hey, kampai!~
Many of you have seen me around the forums and probably know me, but if not; hi! I’m Nolan.
(nearly) Every Saturday I get drunk and stream little micro-indie games to see how fun they are and to give feedback from one dev to another.
CHANNEL:
Not Applicable LIVE!
When I go live, I am here. Highlights go on the other channels.
www.youtube.com
STREAM PLAYLIST (past streams’ archive):
The harsh truth is that most of us don’t really make fun games. We usually get tunnel vision about our project that we tend to miss major points of friction that result in the game being unfun. Well, I’m here to help you face that truth. It may sting at first, but it’s only going to make your game better.
Any dev can submit their game and anyone can suggest a game (from any engine, by the way, not just RM!), but there are some rules for submissions.
Spoiler:
SUBMISSION RULES
Most importantly, make sure it is SFW and follow’s Youtube’s Terms of Service. While I have no problem with 18+ games, unfortunately the TOS of Youtube will not allow for such games.
Similarly, if you are aware of adult situations (such as crude language, glorified violence, and traumatic situations) please make sure to inform me so that I can give a proper warning to my audience.
Do not submit private links, such as Google Drive, Mediafire, etc.
No RM games before MV.
*Some exceptions apply*.
The reason is that these games often cause problems with OBS and the stream.
No visual novels. Sorry, these things are boring. Go read a book.
If you wish to submit a game, please use one of the below methods:
Spoiler:
CONTACT METHODS
Email:
a.m.dolgas (at) protonmail (dot) com
- I’m a bit slow to reply, but this is my preferred method.
Here on RMW through a PM. Just click my name!
Discord:
nolanalighieri
So come join! I stream every Saturday at 10PM (+9GMT - that’s Japan time.)
Here’s a chart to give you a rough idea of what time that might be for your country.
You can also just subscribe to my channel and you’ll get notified when the next stream will occur in your own timezone!

I had taken a short break from streaming games, but glad to be back in the saddle again. Last night's stream actually covered a wide variety of topics, one of which is addressing a good point
@ImaginaryVillain
had brought up when I had streamed his game
Poppet Quest
a few weeks ago: It's not very fair when I spend 10 minutes chatting nonsense while the game's timer is just ticking away. It's a problem I've known about with my streams, but just never bothered to address properly. So, for today, I adjusted the format to 3 games, each 45 minutes, allowing 10 extra minutes to make up for any time I spend just chatting. It's not a good solution, but it's what I'll use in the mean time. I really want to find some sort of Timer app that I can easily pause/unpause with a hotkey at any time, so I can pause the timer whenever I have a lot of thoughts to share.
So, the 3 games that I streamed are:
Capsule Monster
- Tactics by
@TheLastYuriSamurai
, which was submitted to me by the developer.
Golfella
, a game developed in the Godot engine and is about speed-run, combo golf.
and last but not least:
Rave Heart
by
@Starmage
, which was also submitted to me by the developer.
(Capsule Mon dev & Rave Dev, the written review will be posted on your game's respective store page as soon as I have time.)
And, finally, near the end of the stream, I talk about the often overlooked part of game development: Marketing. In particular, I talk about the importance of a Press Kit/Press Release. I even show off what a well-constructed Press Kit might look like, thanks to an official Press Kit being give to me by the publisher of
I See Red
, Gameforge, which I played on stream a few weeks ago. (Also, shout out to the devs of I See Red, they are really cool guys and received my review really well. I always love to give a shout out to the devs that take the feedback well.)

posts.author: TheAM-Dol

On the one hand, as an RM dev, I can sympathize with that frustration. On the other hand, a consumer of a game isn't going to be so discerning about the limitations of the engine. All they know is that "this game won't let me play it comfortably." So, to put it bluntly: it's not their problem, you just have to solve it.
To clarify something here, I don't push for WASD movement - it's definitely what I prefer. What I really push for is rebindable keys so that people who prefer arrow keys can play comfortably, and people who play WASD can play comfortably, and people who are on different keyboard layouts can play comfortably.
It's also worth noting that (while I would never agree with this philosophy) that maybe your audience and scope of your game just doesn't permit rebindable keys. If most of your players are Old Skool RPG players and/or primarily RM-game players, then they probably don't care about WASD, and those that do are a minority.
(You should still cater to the minority to foster goodwill and loyalty with your customers if you plan on being a game dev for a long time, but that's just my opinion.)
Something you may consider looking into is compatibility between VS's keyboard config and other plugins. I assume, like with Yanfly, when you have keyboard config installed alongside other Yanfly plugins, it can take on new properties (such as rebinding keyboard common events), or other plugins may inherit new properties (such as Options Core adding a "Controls" tab)
I would assume if some of VS's plugins utilize W, A, S, or D, then implementing VS keyboard config may allow you adjust those keys.
This is all just an assumption of course, since I don't use MZ or VS plugins.

Dan complains about voice acting

Unpopular(?) opinion, but RPG Maker games
should not
have voice acting.
It's the least reliable type of art to make for indie developers already (why small dev teams try to mimic AAA gaming practices we'll never know), but let's say one of your voice actors has to dip for whatever reason.
Do you remove their lines if they haven't finished, or do you keep it in even though there's blind spots in a game that's otherwise full of voice acting?
Even in the best-case scenario where you have a proper crew of voice actors, you have to orchestrate every single spot where the voice clips have to go and just... it makes me sweat just thinking about all the extra work, hence why I don't bother personally.
I follow a music looping tutorial that uses Audacity, and it's been AMAZING at getting music to loop without playing the opening again. I recorded a copy of the original tutorial in case the user's channel / the video goes down, since you never know what'll happen.

... Why are we poisoning someone for a sidequest? What even is the
main plot?
I still know
nothing
about the main characters.

My main issue is that the maps are built like typical RPG Maker but... it's a tactics game where combat has you walk around the map to fight enemies. It's a confusing blend, since 95% of the tactics games I've played separate their combat screens as unique one-off maps that you can only explore while fighting.
The only exception I can think of is Disgaea, which only has your home base + some bonus maps be freely explorable. Doesn't help that the combat itself is somehow the same old RPG Maker song and dance despite the tactics coat of paint.

TheAM-Dol said:
Dime A Dozen
Click to expand...
I'll just spoiler my thoughts since it's the main reason why I wanted to post to begin with. I'm too busy to play through the game myself, but I still want
@TRIDIUM
to know my thoughts since... well, I want him to succeed and I feel we saw enough to judge during your stream anyway.
Consider this a remote distance review.
Spoiler
* This opening is a clunky loredump. We get zingers like "twelve experiments" and "anomalies can be fused with a human host" before we even know what an anomaly... is? Or are shown a reason to care about their existence?
In this particular scene, it feels like we should have known ahead of time what an anomaly is... even though it seems this is the first game you've released.
It's a common mistake you often see out of indie devs because, well, you got all these big fancy worldbuilding ideas in your head but the execution doesn't pan out the way it should.
Recommendation
: Maybe nix the scene. Or put it later down the line with proper context. As it stands, it's not a very good cold open.
* In fact, I feel it should have started off with the guy and his friend about to narrate. Maybe make that a mite longer and put in actual small story details about what the anomalies are supposed to be, like "they came from outer space back in the medieval ages and sucked everyone's brains" before his friend cuts him off being like "bro how many times are you going to re-write this essay".
Since it feels like you were leaning on the comedy/slice of life aspect when you had the two guys at the start.
* I like that you had the car scene to sell the illusion of movement.
* The mapping suffers from pretty severe "very large but not much actually in it" syndrome. The shopping scene in particular, it's just floor and wall with not much else. I recommend looking up actual grocery stores (or well, room layouts in general) and using them as references, as well as shrinking the maps a bit.
As well as decorating them so they look like actual places and not just abstract video game spaces.
* ... Like Nolan said, you should really do some research on Japan. You're using a sci-fi version of a real place as the backdrop, but you still have to do your dues and make it authentic.
* Observation, but: Are you using Galv's Camera Slide? Because I recognize this camera moving speed.
* Does the stammering girl have a condition or she supposed to be the ultra shy "uwu waifu" character? Because if it's the latter, that's... a big yikes because it's not charming or cute. It's just kind of hilarious. If it's the former, I would recommend researching someone that's stuck with that particular condition.
*
OOF
. I can say without a doubt that this lighting is a catastrophe.
- The darkness is too extreme. It's appropriate to not be able to see anything in pitch black rooms, but if there's light sources like the neon signs outside/inside the bar,
then the map around them should be illuminated, even just a little bit
.
Even then, it's not recommended to make night-time locations in video games so dark you can't see if you want the player to be able to traverse the map - as it stands, it's a bizarre choice that doesn't make sense.
- The inside of the bar is even worse, because the colors are too bright yet they don't actually illuminate the room at all. It needs a
lot
of toning down.
* Before we get into the combat, I just want to comment on the "Zero Dimension" explanation for why your combat has only black screens:
NEVER DO THIS.
Bringing attention to your shortcomings is the worst behavior you could do as a creative, since... well, it's the Streisand Effect in motion. Nobody would have noticed or cared enough if you didn't say anything, but since you made it something the characters themselves brought attention to it stands out much more than it should have had.
It's an extremely common mistake newer creators often do, but moving on since you've already technically fixed it by using the swirly background that VX Ace auto-generates when you don't have battlebacks.
Spoiler:
Just combat
* The combat. Oh man. So I'm normally extremely harsh on peoples' combat in general, but this feels like a fundamental failure of encounter AND mechanics design. To note:
- No tutorial, but you put the player in an encounter where the way to defeat the enemy isn't obvious.
There was a bit I noticed where one guy hit the Hunter with Guard Break and a follow up attack did 155 damage and killed him instantly, whereas before it only did 9. This is
extremely unintuitive
- without an explanation, it just seems like he randomly took more damage than normal... which is a disaster if this is the first enemy you're throwing at the player.
It builds an unhealthy expectation for the rest of the enemies in the game, and... well, guard break mechanics are best used sparingly to begin with, otherwise you'll tire players out from constantly having to deal with them.

, thanks for the feedback!

The hud, like most things is under heavy repairs.

Sorry for the rant!

Hoooboy this was a spicy stream, but by far, one of my favorite streams that I have done yet.

by

Spoiler:
Talking points
Spoiler:
#1: Red Genie Steam page/trailer
This. This is physical proof of how the RTP makes people not take RPG Maker seriously. Where do I begin:
* The fifteen dollar price tag for something that looks like it was whipped up in a few
days
, something that looks worse than the things I've seen people accomplish in a
couple of months.
(re: Berry)
- My jaw fell to the floor when you brought up that Hollow Knight also costs 15 dollars, since... well, Hollow Knight has so much going for it that I'm surprised it's
only
that much. Even if you don't particularly like it, it is an extremely competently designed game for an indie team and deserves its price point.
This does not.
* It's not even a trailer, it's literally just the guy playing the game. It's so low effort it borders on parody - he's just walking across ugly RTP maps and participates in Generic RPG Maker Combat. It has
some
Yanfly plugins, but nothing is fundamentally changed and it just looks like a typical "mash A to win" slugfest.
Spoiler:
#2: RarelyTypicalPlayers Podcast review
(For starters - D7? Why would you even mention that you pirated his game? Such a boneheaded move lmao. Even if you don't like him, that's just something that makes you look bad.)
So let me just say I took the time to see how the RarelyTypicalPlayers review of Red Genie actually went + how the game itself actually functioned:
* Bland nothing-burger intro. No idea who these characters are, don't know why this bartender guy has so many lines like he's an important character.
* Uh oh, it has that annoying thing where you exit the map onto an exit tile, so moving right or left takes you back!
* Bad mapping - layout is often flat + uninteresting + the cliche RPG Maker large empty rooms. Not helped by the high amount of random encounters.
* The only thing that's somewhat interesting is that you can swap equipment on the fly, but given how boneless the combat is... there's no point, since all you really need is the biggest stat stick to whack enemies with. The "guess the weakness with your weapons" thing is also not engaging - it's something that you use to
complement
a combat system, not be the core of it.
We also run into the issue of having to remember what your 14 weapons do during combat.
- If this guy
REALLY DID
go out and get a bachelor's in game design, then I don't see it anywhere in his work. There's no attempt to do anything but the bare minimum an RPG is expected to do - no clever twists, nothing that stops the player from just mashing A to victory, no attention to enemy design, etc.
* The story and characters are pretty much not there. Throughout the entire video playthrough I didn't see anything of substance, not even a cool idea here and there. The main character has no personality, NPCs are just exposition machines, the world is the same generic RTP medieval landscape seen anywhere else.
That one scene where you literally speedrun through plot points. He just did not give a
.
------------------
TLDR; If I have to be brutally honest? Asking 15 dollars for something most of us can make in a week at most (and with better mechanics) kind opens this guy up to get laughed at.
Because the RarelyTypicalPlayers podcast guys were offering legitimate criticism the entire time - there was only really two instances where they outright say the game is garbage, but it's justifiable given the pricing point + they have many, many points to back up their reasoning. Like the combat and the mapping.
But, oh... the dev's reaction is what completes all of this.
Spoiler:
#3: The clip of you reacting to the Red Genie Developer
His reaction to criticism is disgraceful, trying to deflect everything the RTP podcast guys are saying as "nitpicking" and constantly assuming their intentions (and getting them wrong).
I think the most infuriating things he says are:
That he's being lambasted for "not following conventions" when he's following every single bad RPG Maker cliche to the letter. Even down to how his game is presented on the Steam page. It does not look appealing no matter what excuse he uses.
The part where he says "they didn't like my game because it's ambiguous and is supposed to make you think" even though the writing of his game is barebones. It's extremely pretentious thinking (even if it were good writing), and displays a lack of self-awareness.
Not to mention the little complaints of "I took so much time making the music and spent money to get custom assets!"
Like... Dude, join the club. Anybody making a video game has to invest large amounts of time, effort and money to make something that's -
at bare minimum
- presentable.
The most important lesson I learned during my time as a content creator is that the result is what people will see. Excuses accomplish nothing, since it's time better spent trying to improve your craft. But the only thing this dude really accomplished was shooting his marketability in the foot.
I swear I have no beef with this guy (literally did not know who he was until you guys covered him), but can you imagine if he was a bigger name and he acted like this? This would be a PR disaster in every sense of the word.

Just got back from a short holiday. Trying to catch up with everyone who played The Wrath of the Goose King. Thanks again for checking out the game and talking about it, we agreed even before privately that's it probably not your cup of tea, so I'm not that surprised by what you wrote.

Just to correct a few things that were incorrectly stated/overlooked in the video:
- There is a mouse hover effect over the things you can click. (not on the menu though, for example on the choice window)
- You can click on the bubbles over the enemy heads to see what reward each battle holds (it is not pointed out though that's true!)
- There was a chance to equip stuff after shopping, you just clicked continue immediately
- There was also a misunderstanding with Renew. It heals at the end OF EACH turn for 15% for 7 turns. So it's like a full heal over 7 turns
So yeah, as I said earlier, I could tell that this game wasn't your cup of tee, still thanks for checking it out though! Here are some of my thoughts that come up while watching you play:
This is not an attack spam type of game.
As you said in the video, there are no basic attacks, so you need to plan around more on what abilities to use. It takes some time to figure out how some spell actually behave.
I think this is fun for people who like to experiment
with different builds and synenegies: we have over a 100 abilities, 12 pandamembers and over 100 equipment pieces to try out. Not all of them are ground breaking, but it let's you try a lot of different stuff and it feels good when you can make your build feel OP.
You also didn't utilize your abilities the best way (for example, you didn't spend your Fury/TP at all, just sitting with full TP on the main charter at all times
). I'm just pointing this out, because you wrote here that you also didn't enjoy the combat that much. So again: the game rewards those who spend time reading through their abilities and better plan their options. I know that not everyone wants to do this, I simply don't want people to have wrong expectations!
Regarding the story: cutscenes you have seen before are automatically skipped during your future runs! This makes future runs a LOT faster. You also have the option to reset cutscenes if you want to see the story again, or if you want to see it together in one go when you are confident enough to win.
There is only one thing I feel was a bit unfair though, and that's the video's cover image, stating
overpriced
with huge red letters over one of our characters and game's name in the title. After watching the video, I know that this for the other game featured in your video, but it is misleading in my opinion. (Our game will be sold for 6.99 USD with a sale when it comes out) So if the cover picture and the title of the video could be changed a bit, we would very much appreciate it!
So to summ it up: I recommend this game for people who like to spend their sweet time with games: learning new strategies, trying out different builds and don't mind dying before they figure things out. Those people will definitely have fun it!

game, On a Journey this weekend! I had actually been looking forward to this one since I have been keeping up with it's development pretty much ever since he made a development thread here on RMW.
So, I'd say it is still very early. There are a lot of small things that could be fixed, but I would say there are 2 major things that really hold this game back:
Performance
Audio
The performance of the game absolutely sucks, with tons of hitches on scene transfers coupled with really long load times between those transfers, frame rates would be inconsistent, and fluctuate wildly from 144 on one map to 20 on another map.
These major performance problems I think would ruin the game's success in the long run, so I hope there are major plans to fix this.
Secondly is audio. The sound effects used are pretty weak. That isn't always a bad thing, but it does create an obvious disconnect between the quality of the art and the (lack of) quality in the sound. There is quite a wide rift between those 2. It also isn't just sfx, but also mic and voice acting quality. Burly-boy Uther sounds like the guy was recording his lines on a fishing line and cardboard box, once again, juxtaposing the disparity in quality between art and audio.
The good news is, this didn't really ruin my hope for the future of the game, I'm still looking forward to the final release.
One big question remains is the actual combat of the game; the demo gave a pretty controlled and linear progression for the RPG-ness of the characters, which didn't allow me to see how gearing and skills may come into play later in the game. Overall, it wasn't a great impression of the combat, but I also feel like it wasn't a complete picture of the combat either.

I think is the winner
I genuinely lost track of time playing it. And the ending really made it all worth it. I guess my only complaint would be that the intro is a little long, especially when story is not a key point of the game. But considering you put it together in 24 hours, I think this is really well done.
@TRIDIUM
Your game is cute, but it's annoying that it ends the game after you "date" someone. I almost wish you leaned into the absurdity of dating
everyone
approximately 1/3 of the characters - maybe adding a score board, and letting it run continuously. Writing got some good chuckles (and eye rolls) out of me.
@TeiRaven
I like the writing, but the game play was tremendously dull - I'm so sorry Tei
I'm afaid this one just isn't my cup of tea.
@bgillisp
It was a deployment of RPG Maker, yes. I'm not sure what else to say beyond that. I had fun f/cking around with my reverb pedal?
@Sword_of_Dusk
I like the concept of the game, I would certainly love to have a brain tickler mystery for a game, but I'm not sure this one was doing it for me. It didn't really feel like - as the player - I really needed to think too much about the evidence. I also cut it out in the video, but there were a couple of times I just didn't know what to do. It seems the game is a little bit too tightly controlled on flags and player actions, instead of letting the player just assess the crime scene on their own intuition.
@Eliaquim
A lot of other jam games seemed more like visual novels (bg, lol), so I appreciate the attempt to make an actual game. However, it seemed really janky and unforgiving. But I appreciate the good boy.
There were also a handful of games I played on my own time while note recording, so if you're not included here, don't feel too left out (just mostly left out)
